reviewMethod: Complete returned segment lists checked against locked claims, reasons, inferences and quotations; external historical and theological truth is not established by transcription.

reviews.rationale: Hitchens argues that the texts themselves praise Abraham's willingness to sacrifice his son and command destruction and captive-taking. Both eligible quotations are supported in his uninterrupted voice. The end padding introduces settlers but is not credited as an additional selected premise.

Sharpton distinguishes rejection of scriptures from denial of an ordering being, then asks who decides morality without a governor. Every eligible quotation is supported. Brief moderator turn management and Hitchens's separability question are distinguishable from Sharpton's substantive reply; the con transition at the end is not attributed to Sharpton.

Hitchens gives the Samaritan, cooperative species survival, Sinai and golden-rule examples to argue that basic morality precedes religious command. Every eligible phrase is supported. The fragmented opening cross-talk is not part of the selected inference; the sustained argument is consistently Hitchens's voice.
